problem: Prior language-guided navigation setups such as R2R instruction-following assume the requester gives detailed step-by-step route instructions once, at the start. The agent gets no further help when it becomes lost. Standard imitation learning also assumes a teacher that exists only at training time and intervenes directly by overriding actions.
motivation: In realistic deployments the requester often does not know the route and only states an end-goal such as 'Find a cup in one of the bathrooms'. A more knowledgeable human could still help mid-task through language if the agent knows when to ask. The paper argues that an agent should (a) ground high-level object/room goals in vision, (b) sense when it is lost and spend a limited help budget, and (c) interpret language subgoals. Interpreting language subgoals is an indirect intervention, which is not modeled by existing IL frameworks.
key_idea: Formulate object-goal navigation with a test-time advisor as Imitation Learning with Indirect Intervention (I3L): the agent learns a help-request policy under a budget, and the advisor's language subgoal (the next k teacher actions) is prepended to the end-goal as new environment input, trained with Behavior Cloning Under Interventions (BCUI).
insight: Making help-requesting a learned, agent-aware policy matters far more than simply having an advisor. On test unseen, Learned reaches 34.50% SR vs 25.05% for Random-ask and 20.00% for First-ask under the same budget (No-ask: 6.36%). Imitating a heuristic teacher is nearly lossless (Learned 34.50 vs Teacher 34.95). Subgoals are useful as informative input features even when the advisor intervenes directly: a direct advisor with subgoals gets 34.56% vs 32.19% without subgoals on test unseen. The rule ablation shows the useful help-request signals are those computable at test time without ground truth: confusion (entropy), being stuck, and budget ≥ remaining steps together give 35.52% unseen, vs 34.50% with all rules. The GT-dependent rules (deviation from the shortest path, stopping at the goal) barely help and are hard to learn on Matterport3D's small scale.
method: I3L framework: the agent keeps a main (navigation) policy and a help-request policy; a train-time-only teacher coexists with an always-present advisor, whose interventions modify the environment (language subgoal) instead of overriding actions, introducing an intervention-interpretation error.

BCUI training: for the k steps after a help request the agent acts with the teacher's action (behavior cloning), so it never diverges from the subgoal; otherwise it samples from its own policy (IL-style). Both policies are updated online with a max-likelihood loss on teacher actions.

Navigation module: LSTM encoder-decoder with multiplicative attention and coverage. It encodes the (subgoal ⊙ end-goal) text and takes as input ResNet-152 ImageNet features of the current RGB view plus embeddings of the last nav and help actions. It runs two decoding passes: a tentative distribution before the help decision and a final distribution after it.

Help-request module: 1-hidden-layer ReLU MLP over [visual feature; budget embedding; tentative nav distribution; tentative decoder and attention states]. It is trained by behavior cloning of a heuristic teacher, with no backprop into its input features.

Heuristic help-request teacher: requests help if (a) deviation from the shortest path > δ=8 m, (b) the entropy gap to uniform < ε=1.0 (confused), (c) stuck at the same viewpoint for μ=9 steps, (d) budget ≥ remaining steps, or (e) at the goal but argmax is forward.

Advisor and budget: the advisor converts the next k=4 shortest-path teacher actions into templated language (e.g., 'turn 60 degrees left, go forward 2 steps'). The help budget is B = T̂·τ/k with τ=0.4, stochastically rounded. The test-time time budget T̂ is a 95% upper bound estimated from training trajectories between start and goal room types (max 25).

AskNav dataset: templated end-goals 'Find [O] in [R]' over 289 object labels and 26 room labels on Matterport3D (R2R env splits), with success defined as stopping within 2 m of any goal-object viewpoint.

setting.backbone: LSTM encoder-decoder with attention and coverage over frozen ImageNet ResNet-152 features, plus an MLP help-request module (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: AskNav train split: 94,798 data points / 139,757 goals from 61 Matterport3D training environments (templated object-in-room end-goals; teacher actions from shortest paths). A NoRoom variant (78,011 data points / 136,835 goals) is used for the transfer experiment.
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (mean-pooled ResNet-152 feature of the current view) + language end-goal/subgoals; no map, pose, or GPS given to the agent
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph actions: left/right/up/down (30° camera rotation), forward (move to a neighboring viewpoint), stop; plus help actions request/do_nothing
setting.privileged: By task design, an advisor with perfect knowledge (GT map and shortest path) supplies k=4-step language subgoals at test time, within a budget of τ=0.4. The test-time step budget is estimated from training-set trajectory lengths between room types. The agent itself receives no GT pose or map.

numbers_note: The 'Test seen' split has no matching allowed split label, so it is recorded as split 'test' with 'Test seen' stated in extra. All numbers are means over 5 evaluation seeds with 95% CIs (only the means are copied). Dev-split results are not reported. A single-seed qualitative analysis gives 52.0% (test seen) / 34.5% (test unseen). Per-object, per-room and per-path-length results are given only in figures.
results: On AskNav test unseen, the learned help-requesting agent reaches 34.50% SR (NE 5.66 m) vs 6.36% for No-ask, 20.00% for Ask-first and 25.05% for Random-ask under the same budget. On test seen it reaches 52.09% vs 28.39% / 40.33% / 42.98%. This nearly matches the ground-truth-assisted heuristic Teacher policy (34.95% / 52.26%). Subgoals add more than 2% SR on test unseen even with a direct advisor. An AskNav-trained agent finds objects without room hints far better than a Random-ask agent trained for that setting (41.63 vs 33.41 on test unseen).
limitations: The advisor is simulated with perfect knowledge and templated action-level language ('turn 60 degrees right, go forward 2 steps'), not natural human dialogue; results depend on test-time GT-based assistance, so they are not comparable to unassisted ObjectNav/VLN numbers.
BCUI's behavior cloning during subgoal execution creates a train-test mismatch. The GT-dependent help-request rules (a),(e) are hard to learn and even hurt unseen performance at δ=8.
Uses a discrete Matterport3D nav graph with single-view ResNet features and small-scale data (61 train envs); no real-robot or continuous-environment evaluation.
